sectionText:
Lea el texto y responda las preguntas.

En las preguntas \(41 - 45\), marque \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) o \(D\) en su hoja de respuestas.

Does something about living abroad seem extraordinary to you? I understand. That’s what inspired me to leave America for the first time and set out on my journey to start high school in France. However, I was shocked that there were several things I had absolutely no idea about until I landed in France and took part in daily activities there.

Before I arrived, I had only experienced foreign exchange students coming to America, never being one. All those students spoke other languages unknown to me. For me, as an English speaker, that was not the case. Once in France, most of my foreign partners spoke English. In some ways, it’s positive that people communicate with you in your own language because it’s convenient. The disadvantage is you never have that secret moment where you can say things, and no one can imagine what you’re saying.

It will feel shocking to install yourself in a new family’s house, but you can handle this. As you start getting along with them, you can start doing things the way you like them, and it gets cozy. However, there are some things you can’t do your usual way. It’s those little things that separate your life in your home country from your life abroad.

If you’re thinking about doing this, my advice is “say yes more than you say no.” Of course, there will be times when it is acceptable to say no, but if you’re turning down a weekend of excitement with your classmates or your family there, you’re not taking advantage of your exchange. Part of the reason you are living this adventure is to experience things. Say yes and you will not be disappointed.
questionText: Pregunta 44: What makes life abroad different from life at home is
aiExplanation:
- **Core problem:** Identify what the text says separates life abroad from life at home.
- **Relevant data:** The writer says there are some things you cannot do your usual way, and *those little things* separate life at home from life abroad.
- **Method:** Choose the option that paraphrases changing everyday habits.
- **Conclusion:** The difference is **the habits you must change to get on with your new life**. The correct answer is **C**.

options.optionFeedback: - **Incorrect.** The text does not describe the people abroad as unkind.
- **Incorrect.** Living in a new house is part of the experience, but the text emphasizes everyday things you cannot do your usual way.

options.optionText: the habits you must change to get on with your new life.
options.optionFeedback: - **Correct.** This directly reflects the idea that little everyday differences and changed routines separate life abroad from life at home.

options.optionText: the time it takes to have a friendly relationship with the homeowners.
options.optionFeedback: - **Incorrect.** The text says you can eventually get along with the family, but that is not the main difference highlighted.
